lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the ecosystem has a direct, active precedent plus a hostile-but-mappable upstream. (1) Precedent fork weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive (v0.1.17, base vLLM 0.21.0, CUDA 12.8, torch 2.11.0+cu128, 2026-active, 815 stars): dual 22 GB RTX 2080 Ti + NVLink, TP=2, primary route Qwen3.x 27B (Qwen3.6/3.8) with FP8 / AWQ-INT4 / GPTQ-INT4 / NVFP4 / Quark-INT8 / AutoRound weights, KV cache in FP16 / INT8 / TurboQuant K8V4, MTP3 speculative presets, native 256K context, multimodal image; measured 100+ tok/s single-request decode on Qwen3.6-27B FP8, ~91 tok/s on an i3-9100T host vs ~56 tok/s on Xeon X5675 (GPTQ-INT4, MTP3, 4096/128); secondary route Qwen3.x 35B MoE (35B-A3B FP8: 256K text-only, 136K text+image, 178K MTP3 fast preset); Gemma4 31B experimental (QAT w4a16). Its hardware FAQ explicitly names Quadro RTX 6000 24 GB (this host's card) as a good TU102 candidate, TITAN RTX and RTX 8000 too. Its serving philosophy is single-concurrency personal-agent workloads with long prefill serialized by the scheduler on the TP=2 profile - directly relevant to preemption coupling. Prefill uses a FlashQLA sm70/sm75 adaptation (weicj/FlashQLA-SM70-SM75) for the GDN linear-attention layers plus FlashInfer. Checkpoints named: QuantTrio/Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ, llmfan46 GPTQ-int4 with native MTP preserved, unsloth NVFP4. (2) Upstream vLLM: v0.14.0 (2026-01-20) shipped "Marlin for Turing (sm75)" (#29901, #31000) restoring W4A16 GPTQ/AWQ on T4/2080Ti-class, plus NVFP4 Marlin MoE (#30881), MXFP4 W4A16 dense (#31926), async scheduling as default (composable with MTP spec decode), and --max-model-len auto; v0.21.0 is the fork base generation; v0.23.0 is the last-good FlashInfer-on-sm75 release (FP8 KV works); v0.24.0 (July 2026) dropped FlashInfer from the SM7.5 candidate list - issue #47549 (opened 2026-07-03, 18x Quadro RTX 8000 fleet, still open) documents the full failure chain: FP8 KV loss -> KV capacity halved (287,744 -> ~143,000 tokens) -> preemption storms at long context -> decode at 22K ctx collapsing from 5-11 to 0.8-1.1 tok/s (5-10x); workaround is pinning the v0.23.0 container. (3) KV compression: TurboQuant (Google Research + NYU, ICLR 2026; blog 2026-03, arXiv 2504.19874) achieves near-lossless 3-bit KV with no fine-tuning; community ports exist (AmesianX/TurboQuant: 1M-token KV in ~9.6 GB, MTP-compatible; llama.cpp discussions #20969/#21155; vLLM study 2026-05-11); vLLM mainline exposes turboquant_4bit_nc as a kv-cache-dtype but it is attention-backend-coupled and currently broken - #40094 (2026-04-17, L4 GPU, open, no response) shows TRITON_ATTN and FLASH_ATTN both rejecting it. (4) KTransformers (kvcache-ai, ACM paper DOI 10.1145/3731569.3764843 [uncertain: ktransformers_paper_year], SGLang integration since 2025-10-22 per lmsys.org blog, v0.7.0 on 2026-08-17): CPU-resident MoE experts + GPU attention/shared experts, AMX/AVX512/AVX2 CPU backends, accelerators listed are 4090/L20-class NVIDIA, Intel Arc, ROCm, Ascend - Turing not mentioned [uncertain: ktransformers_sm75_support]. Its leaderboard (2026-09) tops out at Qwen3.5-35B-A3B FP8: 97.5 tok/s decode on 4x RTX 5090 + 2x EPYC 9355, 86.2 on 1x 5090, 19.3 on 1x 4090 + AVX2 EPYC; Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 52.5 on 1x 5090; DeepSeek-R1-0528 FP8 227.85 total / 87.58 output tok/s on 8x L20 + Xeon Gold. It targets MoE models; the dense-GDN-hybrid 27B is not in its model list, so on this host it is only a candidate for the 35B-A3B MoE secondary. (5) Interconnect reality: Quadro RTX 6000 pairs get a 2-way NVLink bridge (2 links, ~50 GB/s per direction, ~100 GB/s aggregate per NVIDIA datasheet [uncertain: nvlink_bridge_datasheet_bandwidth]; this host measured 43.7 GB/s on the plan/0004 cross-GPU K-shard); GeForce Turing needs the bridge for any P2P at all (NVIDIA blocks PCIe P2P on GeForce; Quadro keeps it); NCCL exposes NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL and NCCL_P2P_DISABLE knobs; the bridge topology is terminal - RTX 6000 Ada dropped NVLink [uncertain: rtx_6000_ada_no_nvlink]. (6) Target-model geometry (HF Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 config.json fetched 2026-09-07; config carries model_type qwen3_5 [uncertain: qwen36_27b_config_provenance]): 64 layers = 48 GDN linear-attention + 16 full-attention (interval 4), full attention 24 Q heads / 4 KV heads / head_dim 256, GDN 16 K-heads / 48 V-heads at 128/128 dims with fp32 SSM state, max context 262,144, one MTP hidden layer - matching plan/0007's 75%-GDN / d256 / d128 description exactly.
lacuna.sm75_viability: It runs today, with measured numbers on two independent Turing fleets. (a) This host (2x Quadro RTX 6000, fork engine): plan/0007 2026-09-06 gate - Qwen3.6-27B-AutoRound W4A16, TP=2, MML 40960, all 14 engine gates pass, PPL 2k 6.7761 (plan/0006 record drift 0.0002), d256 full-attention layers routed to BRIDGE_ATTN on both ranks, 512-token long decode clean at ctx up to 32768; known warts: tp2 decode swings 12.4-16.4 tok/s between engine restarts of the same kernel, and under cross-restart medians tp2 bridge decode sits at 0.85-0.90 of seeded (engine-level lockstep deficit, bisect open). (b) The precedent fork on strictly weaker hardware (2080 Ti: 4352 cores, 616 GB/s, 22 GB vs RTX 6000: 4608 cores, 672 GB/s, 24 GB + Quadro P2P): 100+ tok/s single-request decode Qwen3.6-27B FP8 with MTP3 + TurboQuant K8V4 KV, and it validated running even on non-ideal PCIe (x1 + x4) with NVLink merely recommended. W4A16 kernel floor: INT4 tensor-core math does not exist on sm75 (ptxas rejects s4 mma, MEMORY 2026-08-27), so all 4-bit paths dequantize in registers - upstream sm75 Marlin (v0.14.0+) and this fork's staged/regdequant family both do; NVFP4-on-Marlin is nominally CC>=75 but reported garbage on real Turing (#33461, sibling item). Attention-backend candidate matrix on sm75 as of 2026-09: FLASHINFER (works through v0.23.0 and in the fork; the only upstream path that carried FP8/INT8 KV on sm75; removed from candidates in v0.24.0), TRITON_ATTN (always-present fallback per vllm.ai deep-dive 2026-03-04; FMA-bound codegen from Triton >=3.3 and it rejects quantized/TurboQuant kv-cache dtypes - #40094), BRIDGE_ATTN (this fork, owns d256), FLASH_ATTN (sm80+), FLEX_ATTENTION (listed in this fork's candidate set). GDN linear side: FLA Triton kernels run but are FMA-bound; weicj/FlashQLA-SM70-SM75 proves a forward-inference-only sm75 GDN kernel exists. KV-capacity envelope for the operator's model (16 full-attn layers x 4 KV heads x head_dim 256 = 32,768 KV elements/token; GDN layers contribute zero per-token KV): per-token KV = 64 KiB fp16 / 32 KiB int8 or fp8 / 24 KiB K8V4 / 16 KiB K4V4 / ~12 KiB at 3-bit; equivalently 16,384 / 32,768 / 43,691 / 65,536 / ~87,400 tokens per GiB. The GDN recurrent state is context-independent but per-sequence: 48 layers x 48 V-heads x 128 x 128 x fp32 = 144 MiB/sequence (72 MiB if fp16 state), which caps concurrency (~100-200 concurrent seqs on a 15-20 GiB KV budget) independently of context. With W4A16 ~14-15 GB weights + overhead, 2x24 GB leaves ~26-30 GiB aggregate KV: ~430-490K tokens fp16, ~860-980K int8/fp8, ~1.1-1.3M K8V4, ~1.7-2.0M at 4-bit; a single 256K-token context costs 16 GiB fp16 / 8 GiB int8 / 6 GiB K8V4 - native 256K is feasible on 48 GB exactly as the fork ships it on 44 GB. TP=2 shards the 4 KV heads 2+2 (aggregate unchanged, half per card; 4 KV heads are divisible by TP=2 but not by TP=8-class sharding). Note the hybrid architecture's structural advantage: 64 KiB/token fp16 is ~8x lighter than a classic dense 64-layer/8-KV-head model (~0.5 MiB/token, the #47549 fleet's class). Preemption coupling: vLLM V1 defaults to RECOMPUTE preemption (docs v0.18.1 + discuss.vllm.ai #1672); the demonstrated chain is capacity loss -> preemption storms -> 5-10x decode collapse at 22K ctx (#47549), and arXiv 2411.07447 measures up to 30% throughput degradation from preempting long requests (40% latency reduction when avoided); the trap is silent - backend fall-through to TRITON_ATTN quietly drops the KV dtype, halving capacity before any alarm. KTransformers on 2x Turing + host CPU: unproven [uncertain: ktransformers_sm75_support] - no sm75 mention in README or leaderboard, CPU side wants AMX/AVX512 for throughput (19.3 tok/s on AVX2 EPYC + 1x 4090 is the cautionary datapoint), and it targets MoE, so it is the fallback topology for the 35B MoE secondary, not the dense-GDN 27B primary.
lacuna.upstream_base: Dated sm75 ledger lines for this surface: 2025 v0.11.1 re-enabled FP16 on Turing via FlashInfer (per outline); 2026-01-20 v0.14.0 - "Marlin for Turing (sm75)" #29901/#31000 (W4A16 GPTQ/AWQ dense + MoE on sm75 upstream; the fork can rebase its W4A16 lane onto this), NVFP4 Marlin MoE #30881, MXFP4 W4A16 dense #31926, deprecated quant schemes removed #31688, async scheduling default (MTP-compatible), --max-model-len auto #29431, wheel moves to cu129/torch 2.9.1; v0.21.0 - the precedent fork's base generation (CUDA 12.8 / torch 2.11 stack); v0.23.0 - last-good FlashInfer-on-sm75, i.e. the last upstream release where FP8/INT8 KV dtype survives on this hardware [uncertain: vllm_v0.23_v0.24_release_dates]; v0.24.0 (July 2026) - FlashInfer removed from SM7.5 candidates, regression #47549 open with no fix, documented workaround is pinning vllm-openai:v0.23.0. Recommended bases for the fork: keep the retained-Turing-engine fork (v0.21.0-class) as serving base; take upstream kernel rows (sm75 Marlin family) by cherry-pick; do not rebase the engine past v0.23.0 until FlashInfer is restored or an explicit --attention-backend override lands. Peripheral pins: NCCL 2.31.x (NCCL_P2P_LEVEL/NCCL_P2P_DISABLE documented), Triton <=3.2 for sm75 tensor-core health (>=3.4 needed only for MXFP4 tl.dot_scaled emulation - sibling deadlock item).

effort_value.effort_estimate: A full stage-13 campaign but not a kernel campaign - all kernel lanes already exist (plan/0002 W4A16 staged, plan/0007 d256 bridge, fork engine). Scope: (a) NVLink/P2P + NCCL validation on the pair (nvidia-smi topo -m NV2, p2pBandwidthLatencyTest, NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL), 0.5-1 day; (b) serving-config matrix - weights format (AutoRound W4A16 / AWQ / FP8-recast) x KV dtype (fp16 / int8 / K8V4 if wired) x MTP3 on/off - capturing startup 'GPU KV cache size' token counts and asserting the engaged attention backend per arm, 2-3 days; (c) preemption envelope probe at 22K+ context (single long request + prefix cache, max-num-seqs sweep, preemption counters), 1-2 days; (d) committed tokens/s benchmark under the plan/0007 cross-restart median-of-5 discipline, 2-3 days incl. transcripts beside results/gate_results/b27_tp2_sweep.json; (e) optional KTransformers side-evaluation for the 35B MoE secondary, 1-2 days. Total roughly 1.5-2 weeks single-operator.
effort_value.unlocks: The plan/0005 milestone acceptance itself (27B-class checkpoint loads, generates on both cards, tokens/s committed); native 256K-class long-context serving on 48 GB via the KV envelope (int8/fp8 KV or K8V4); the 35B-A3B MoE secondary route; a measured TP-over-NVLink vs plan/0004 shard-strategies (43.7 GB/s K-shard) decision for every future ~30B model on this host; a production-shaped workload that feeds the tp2-decode-variance/lockstep bisect (sibling item) with the exact case it needs; and, if KTransformers proves viable, a CPU+RAM escape hatch for models beyond 48 GB.
effort_value.dependency_order: Already landed (no re-work needed): Turing-capable engine (stage 11, retained in fork), W4A16 staged strategy + AutoRound adapter (stages 3-4, plan/0002 lane), d256 bridge attention with 27B routing proven on both ranks (plan/0007, 2026-09-06). Sequential-first ideal: the plan/0007 tp2 lockstep bisect (per-tile barrier vs staging under TP2) - its 0.85-0.90 deficit directly caps the stage-13 headline number - but stage 13 can run in parallel and generate the engine-level traces the bisect needs (nsys/ncu on tp2 decode). External prerequisites: NVLink P2P verified at driver level (topo NV2 + p2pBandwidthLatencyTest), HF checkpoints present (QuantTrio/Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ, llmfan46 GPTQ-int4 MTP-preserved, unsloth NVFP4). Parallelizable immediately: KV-capacity envelope table (pure geometry math + startup-log reconciliation), KTransformers MoE evaluation (independent stack), TurboQuant K8V4 KV integration (gated by the fp8-kv-and-activations / TurboQuant sibling item and by backend support - #40094 shows the upstream dtype path is broken, so the fork path is the realistic one).
effort_value.risk_notes: (1) tp2 decode restart variance 12.4-16.4 tok/s on identical kernels (plan/0007): without median-of-N-across-restarts the committed number is luck; NCCL transport selection at communicator init is the suspected per-restart variable. (2) The tp2 lockstep deficit (0.85-0.90 of seeded, stable across restarts) is unexplained - worst case TP=2 loses to single-card W4A16 with the second card serving a second instance, which changes the milestone's serving topology. (3) Silent KV-dtype/backend fallback: fall-through to TRITON_ATTN silently drops FP8/INT8 KV (2x capacity cliff) and preemption storms follow (#47549 chain); gates must assert selected-backend + engaged-kv-dtype strings in transcripts. (4) Numerics: W4A16 asymmetric+ZP unpacking is a known bug surface (compressed-tensors #458 class); int8/TurboQuant KV quality is statistical - gate on logprob deltas vs fp16 KV per context length, not PPL alone; TurboQuant upstream dtype path is immature (#40094 open, unmaintained). (5) GDN state footprint (144 MiB/seq fp32) can surprise concurrency ceilings even when KV tokens look plentiful. (6) Upstream drift: v0.24.0+ removed the only sm75 backend that carries quantized KV - every rebase window that passes widens the fork gap; MTP3 on sm75 has no upstream benchmark (#21278-class evidence spec decode can fail to pay on constrained GPUs). (7) KTransformers on sm75 is unvalidated and may hard-fail on architecture floors; treat as experiment, not plan.
effort_value.determinism_class: Mixed. Bitwise-clean parts: W4A16 weight dequant is exact (integer values x scales; float64-oracle attests loader and kernel identically); E4M3->FP16 recast is lossless. Statistical parts: NCCL allreduce reduction order is fixed per topology/algorithm but transport selection at per-restart communicator init varies (the observed 12.0-17.5 tok/s swings), so tokens/s is a statistical quantity - gate on median-of-5 samples across >=3 engine restarts (plan/0007 methodology fix, 2026-09-07); KV quantization is per-token/head rounding - acceptance is a logprob-delta distribution vs fp16 KV, median over N sequences per context bucket; preemption/recompute is deterministic for a fixed schedule but prefix-cache state and arrival order make end-to-end runs distributed - fix seeds, prompt set, and cache state in benchmarks. Constraint to hold: split-K atomicAdd accumulation under CUDA-graph replay still needs workspace zeroing between replays (sibling item) or restart-to-restart drift contaminates even the oracle lane; the PPL anchor (2k = 6.7761, drift <= 0.0002 vs plan/0006) is the numeric gate that must not move while tuning the serving knobs.

decision.priority_signal: For doing this next: it is the plan/0005 acceptance anchor and the operator's named target; the host already passes all 14 engine gates with the exact model and quant (2026-09-06), so the remaining work is configuration and measurement, not research; the precedent fork proves 100+ tok/s single-request decode on strictly weaker 22 GB 2080 Ti hardware (this host's Quadro RTX 6000 adds ~6% cores, ~9% bandwidth, ECC, Quadro P2P, and 2 GB more per card), which de-risks the headline number; NVLink is measured working on this host (43.7 GB/s K-shard); the checkpoint ecosystem (QuantTrio AWQ, MTP-preserved GPTQ, unsloth NVFP4) and the sibling fork are 2026-active, so technique transfer is cheapest now. Against: the tp2 lockstep deficit (0.85-0.90 of seeded, engine-level, bisect open) directly caps the both-card number and could flip the verdict to single-card-per-instance; upstream v0.24.0 removed the sm75 KV-dtype backend, so every month of delay widens the rebase gap; MTP3's payoff on sm75 is unbenchmarked. Window-closing risk is real but the fork lane already holds a working engine - the exposure is drift, not feasibility. Verdict: do next, sequenced alongside (and feeding) the tp2 variance bisect.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0 style, oracle-first, no timing until numerics pass: (1) Numerics - boot Qwen3.6-27B-AutoRound TP=2 on the fork engine with fp16 KV; assert BRIDGE_ATTN routing strings on both ranks; PPL 2k must land in the 6.7761 +/- 0.0002 band and distinct3 logprobs in the 0.61-0.98 envelope at ctx 512/2048/8192/16384/32768 (reuses the proven plan/0007 gate). (2) Capacity - for each KV arm (fp16, int8, K8V4 if wired) read the startup 'GPU KV cache size' tokens and reconcile against the computed envelope (16,384 / 32,768 / 43,691 tokens/GiB; mismatch or a TRITON_ATTN selection string = silent-fallback caught, zero cost). (3) Preemption - one 22K-context request with prefix cache on, sweep --max-num-seqs downward until vLLM's preemption counters read zero; record the zero-preemption concurrency boundary per dtype - this is the #47549 failure chain measured before it can bite. Only then timing: decode tok/s, median-of-5 across >=3 engine restarts, single-request plus small-batch arms, committed next to results/gate_results/b27_tp2_sweep.json. Kill-switch logic: step (1) already passes per plan/0007, so the probe's real question is (2)+(3) - if the KV arms engage their dtypes and the zero-preemption boundary covers the operator's context/concurrency shape, the stage is a campaign; if the dtype silently falls back, the campaign must first carry the fork's INT8/TurboQuant KV path (sibling item).
